# plug

```go
import "github.com/kitsunium/sdk/framework/internal/app/plug"
```

Package plug is where the framework's opt-in subsystems plug in: the HTTP engine, the frontends' file server and the process sampler of the runtime graph (framework/app/server), the Studio — the tool's variables, its routes and the framework's sentences in the languages after English (framework/app/studio) —, the stores and the databases (framework/app/store), the queues (framework/app/queue), the workflows (framework/app/workflow), the mailers (framework/app/mail), the jobs (framework/app/jobs). The framework reads what they registered through the hooks declared here, and imports none of the SDK packages behind them: a product that does not import a subsystem neither links nor initialises its packages.

It is also the contract between the framework's core and the subsystems ADR 0179 takes out of it, as database/sql/driver is between database/sql and a driver: the store subsystem's engine over documents, its siblings, the framework's scope on a database and its migrations ([Stores](#Stores)), which framework/app/store sets; the refusals an engine says in the framework's terms ([Refusal](#Refusal)); what the framework's transactions offer an engine that takes part in them ([Transaction](#Transaction)); the queue subsystem's brokers and their consumer ([Queues](#Queues)), which framework/app/queue sets; the workflow subsystem's engine and the ports it runs on ([Workflows](#Workflows)), which framework/app/workflow sets; the mail subsystem's outbox and transports ([Mail](#Mail)), which framework/app/mail sets; the jobs subsystem's schedules and scheduler ([Jobs](#Jobs)), which framework/app/jobs sets; the framework's catalogues in the languages after English ([Words](#Words)), and the Studio's routes and the tool's variables ([Studio](#Studio), ADR 0180 step 1), which framework/app/studio sets, the routes reading the running app through a [StudioHost](#StudioHost) the framework gives.

The package imports the standard library and the framework's model only, so that the framework and every subsystem can import it.

## Constants

<a name="LabelLoop"></a>
```go
const LabelLoop string = "app_loop"
```

LabelLoop is the pprof label naming the loop a goroutine belongs to.

<a name="LabelNode"></a>
```go
const LabelNode string = "app_node"
```

LabelNode is the pprof label naming the node a goroutine works for.

<a name="MailEventDeadLettered"></a>
```go
const MailEventDeadLettered MailEvent = 4
```

MailEventDeadLettered is a mail given up on after its last attempt.

<a name="MailEventDuplicate"></a>
```go
const MailEventDuplicate MailEvent = 5
```

MailEventDuplicate is a redelivery of a mail already sent, dropped.

<a name="MailEventOther"></a>
```go
const MailEventOther MailEvent = 0
```

MailEventOther is an event of the spool the framework shows nothing of.

<a name="MailEventQueued"></a>
```go
const MailEventQueued MailEvent = 1
```

MailEventQueued is a mail put in the outbox.

<a name="MailEventRetrying"></a>
```go
const MailEventRetrying MailEvent = 3
```

MailEventRetrying is a failed attempt that will be retried.

<a name="MailEventSent"></a>
```go
const MailEventSent MailEvent = 2
```

MailEventSent is a mail the transport accepted.

<a name="MailGivenUpExhausted"></a>
```go
const MailGivenUpExhausted MailGiveUp = 0
```

MailGivenUpExhausted is a mail whose last attempt failed.

<a name="MailGivenUpExpired"></a>
```go
const MailGivenUpExpired MailGiveUp = 2
```

MailGivenUpExpired is a mail whose attempt failed once it was older than the spool's MaxAge.

<a name="MailGivenUpRejected"></a>
```go
const MailGivenUpRejected MailGiveUp = 1
```

MailGivenUpRejected is a mail the receiving server refused for good, an SMTP 5xx reply, dead-lettered without a retry.

<a name="MailRefusalClosed"></a>
```go
const MailRefusalClosed MailRefusal = 1
```

MailRefusalClosed is a spool that is closed: its mailer is not running.

<a name="MailRefusalInvalidURL"></a>
```go
const MailRefusalInvalidURL MailRefusal = 3
```

MailRefusalInvalidURL is an SMTP URL that is not one of the form smtp://user:password@host:port; its "problem" field says the clause.

<a name="MailRefusalNone"></a>
```go
const MailRefusalNone MailRefusal = 0
```

MailRefusalNone is no refusal the framework words.

<a name="MailRefusalUnencodable"></a>
```go
const MailRefusalUnencodable MailRefusal = 2
```

MailRefusalUnencodable is a mail the outbox cannot encode.

<a name="OTLPBlock"></a>
```go
const OTLPBlock string = "block"
```

OTLPBlock makes the producer wait for room, up to a bound.

<a name="OTLPDropNewest"></a>
```go
const OTLPDropNewest string = "drop-newest"
```

OTLPDropNewest refuses the new batch.

<a name="OTLPDropOldest"></a>
```go
const OTLPDropOldest string = "drop-oldest"
```

OTLPDropOldest takes the oldest batches out until the new one fits.

<a name="OTLPMetrics"></a>
```go
const OTLPMetrics string = "metrics"
```

OTLPMetrics names the metrics signal: an OTLP/JSON ExportMetricsServiceRequest.

<a name="OTLPTraces"></a>
```go
const OTLPTraces string = "traces"
```

OTLPTraces names the trace signal: an OTLP/JSON ExportTraceServiceRequest.

<a name="RefusalClosed"></a>
```go
const RefusalClosed Refusal = 13
```

RefusalClosed is a call on a closed engine.

<a name="RefusalExists"></a>
```go
const RefusalExists Refusal = 2
```

RefusalExists is a document already under the key an insertion names.

<a name="RefusalIndexBroken"></a>
```go
const RefusalIndexBroken Refusal = 8
```

RefusalIndexBroken is stored documents that break a unique index.

<a name="RefusalIndexNotUnique"></a>
```go
const RefusalIndexNotUnique Refusal = 7
```

RefusalIndexNotUnique is a lookup on an index that is not unique.

<a name="RefusalIndexUnknown"></a>
```go
const RefusalIndexUnknown Refusal = 6
```

RefusalIndexUnknown is an index the store does not declare.

<a name="RefusalKeyChanged"></a>
```go
const RefusalKeyChanged Refusal = 5
```

RefusalKeyChanged is an update that changes the document's key.

<a name="RefusalKeyEmpty"></a>
```go
const RefusalKeyEmpty Refusal = 4
```

RefusalKeyEmpty is a document whose key is empty.

<a name="RefusalKeyTooLong"></a>
```go
const RefusalKeyTooLong Refusal = 18
```

RefusalKeyTooLong is a key longer than a database's key columns hold; its "max" field says how long they hold.

<a name="RefusalLoad"></a>
```go
const RefusalLoad Refusal = 12
```

RefusalLoad is a store that could not be loaded; its "problem" field says why.

<a name="RefusalNone"></a>
```go
const RefusalNone Refusal = 0
```

RefusalNone is no refusal the framework words.

<a name="RefusalNotFound"></a>
```go
const RefusalNotFound Refusal = 1
```

RefusalNotFound is no document under the key, or under the index's key.

<a name="RefusalNotTrashed"></a>
```go
const RefusalNotTrashed Refusal = 17
```

RefusalNotTrashed is no record in the trash under the key.

<a name="RefusalOutOfOrder"></a>
```go
const RefusalOutOfOrder Refusal = 22
```

RefusalOutOfOrder is a migration older than one already applied; its "applied" field names the newer.

<a name="RefusalPersist"></a>
```go
const RefusalPersist Refusal = 11
```

## Variables

<a name="Jobs"></a>
```go
var Jobs atomic.Pointer[JobDriverConfig]
```

Jobs is the jobs subsystem: the schedules of the framework's jobs and the scheduler that fires them; nil until framework/app/jobs is imported. A product that declares a job without it is refused at the start (ADR 0179 §6).

<a name="Mail"></a>
```go
var Mail atomic.Pointer[MailDriverConfig]
```

Mail is the mail subsystem: the outbox the framework's mailers keep and the transports that empty it; nil until framework/app/mail is imported. A product that declares a mailer without it is refused at the start (ADR 0179 §6).

<a name="NewHTTPServer"></a>
```go
var NewHTTPServer atomic.Pointer[func(cfg HTTPConfig) HTTPServer]
```

NewHTTPServer builds the HTTP engine an app in the server profile serves on; nil until framework/app/server is imported.

<a name="NewStaticFiles"></a>
```go
var NewStaticFiles atomic.Pointer[func(fsys fs.FS, csp string) (http.Handler, error)]
```

NewStaticFiles builds the file server of a frontend's tree; nil until framework/app/server is imported.

<a name="OTLP"></a>
```go
var OTLP atomic.Pointer[OTLPDriverConfig]
```

OTLP is the OTLP export subsystem; nil until framework/app/otlp is imported. A product that declares app.OTLP without it is refused at the start (ADR 0179 §6).

<a name="Queues"></a>
```go
var Queues atomic.Pointer[QueueDriverConfig]
```

Queues is the queue subsystem: the brokers the framework's consumers' queues run on and the migration of a queue's table on a database; nil until framework/app/queue is imported. A product that declares a topic, a subscription, a watch, a queued command or a mailer whose outbox is on a database without it is refused at the start (ADR 0179 §6).

<a name="SampleProcess"></a>
```go
var SampleProcess atomic.Pointer[func() *model.Process]
```

SampleProcess samples the running process — its heap, goroutines, collections and CPU time — for the runtime graph a serving app answers; nil until framework/app/server is imported, and the graph then carries no process (ADR 0172).

<a name="Stores"></a>
```go
var Stores atomic.Pointer[StoreDriverConfig]
```

Stores is the store subsystem: the engines the framework's stores run on, the framework's scope on a database and the migrations of the framework's tables; nil until framework/app/store is imported. A product that declares a store or a database without it is refused at the start (ADR 0179 §6).

<a name="Studio"></a>
```go
var Studio atomic.Pointer[StudioDriverConfig]
```

Studio is the Studio subsystem: the tool's variables and the Studio's routes; nil until framework/app/studio is imported, and the framework then reads none of the tool's variables and serves no route of the Studio.

<a name="Words"></a>
```go
var Words atomic.Pointer[WordsConfig]
```

Words is the framework's sentences in the languages after English, the catalogues the Studio shows its reader's language from; nil until framework/app/studio is imported, and the framework then speaks English alone. The terminal, the logs and an error read English whatever a program imports (ADR 0179 Q6).

<a name="Workflows"></a>
```go
var Workflows atomic.Pointer[WorkflowDriverConfig]
```

Workflows is the workflow subsystem: the engine the framework's workflows run on; nil until framework/app/workflow is imported. A product that declares a workflow without it is refused at the start (ADR 0179 §6).

<a name="Broker"></a>
## type [Broker](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/framework/internal/app/plug/queue_interface.go>)

Broker is one queue as the framework's core uses it: a publication, the consumer that delivers it, and its dead letters. It grows by the siblings below.

```go
type Broker interface {
	// Consume delivers the queue's messages to cfg's handler until ctx ends
	// or the queue's storage fails.
	Consume(ctx context.Context, cfg ConsumeConfig) error
	// DeadLetters are up to maxLetters of the queue's dead letters, oldest
	// first.
	DeadLetters(ctx context.Context, maxLetters int) ([]DeadLetterValue, error)
	// Publish puts payload in the queue: in the transaction ctx carries for
	// its database, when it lives on one.
	Publish(ctx context.Context, payload []byte) error
}
```


Consume delivers the queue's messages to cfg's handler until ctx ends or the queue's storage fails.

<a name="Clock"></a>
## type [Clock](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/framework/internal/app/plug/queue_interface.go>)

Clock is the app's clock as a queue stamps and waits on it: the framework's core hands the one its app runs on, a test's manual clock included.

```go
type Clock interface {
	// After is a channel that receives the clock's instant once d passed.
	After(d time.Duration) <-chan time.Time
	// NewTicker is a ticker that fires every d.
	NewTicker(d time.Duration) Ticker
	// NewTimer is a timer that fires once d passed.
	NewTimer(d time.Duration) Timer
	// Now is the clock's instant.
	Now() time.Time
	// Since is how long ago t was, on the clock.
	Since(t time.Time) time.Duration
	// Sleep waits until d passed.
	Sleep(d time.Duration)
}
```

<a name="ConsumeConfig"></a>
## type [ConsumeConfig](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/framework/internal/app/plug/queue.go>)

ConsumeConfig is how a queue's consumer runs: its handler, how long it waits idle, how many messages it handles at once and takes at a time, how it stops, whether it renews a running handler's lease, and when a handler asked to be retried.

```go
type ConsumeConfig struct {
	// Handler handles one delivery: nil acknowledges it, an error has it
	// retried or, through DoNotRetry, dead-lettered at once. Every handler
	// the framework runs tolerates a redelivery.
	Handler       func(ctx context.Context, d DeliveryValue) error
	// PollInterval bounds an idle wait.
	PollInterval  time.Duration
	// Parallelism is how many deliveries are handled at once.
	Parallelism   int
	// BatchSize is how many messages the consumer takes at a time.
	BatchSize     int
	// DrainTimeout is how long the handler running when ctx ends may still
	// run before its context is cancelled; zero cancels it at once.
	DrainTimeout  time.Duration
	// SettleTimeout bounds each outcome sent once ctx ended, and each lease
	// renewal; zero is the queue's own bound.
	SettleTimeout time.Duration
	// AutoExtend renews the lease of the message a handler runs for as long
	// as it runs.
	AutoExtend    bool
	// RetryIn reads, from the error a delivery's handler returned, the delay
	// it asked to be retried after: its queue hands the message back with
	// that delay, the delivery counted. Nil, or false, keeps the queue's own
	// retry delay.
	RetryIn       func(err error) (delay time.Duration, asked bool)
}
```

<a name="Database"></a>
## type [Database](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/framework/internal/app/plug/store_interface.go>)

Database is the framework's scope on one database (ADR 0179 §2): the transactions app.Transact opens on it, their savepoints, and the functions held until their end. The core knows a database only through it; the store package implements it over the SDK's sql. It grows by the siblings below.

```go
type Database interface {
	// Defer holds fn until the transaction ctx carries for the database
	// commits, and reports true; outside one it holds nothing and reports
	// false.
	Defer(ctx context.Context, fn func()) bool
	// InTransaction reports whether ctx carries a transaction of this
	// database.
	InTransaction(ctx context.Context) bool
	// OnAbort holds fn until the work of the scope ctx carries for the
	// database is undone, and reports true; outside one it holds nothing
	// and reports false.
	OnAbort(ctx context.Context, fn func(ctx context.Context)) bool
	// Transact runs fn in a transaction of the database, or in a savepoint
	// of the one ctx carries for it: nil commits or releases, an error
	// rolls back.
	Transact(ctx context.Context, fn func(ctx context.Context) error) error
}
```

<a name="Database.Defer"></a>

```go
func (Database) Defer(ctx context.Context, fn func()) bool
```

Defer holds fn until the transaction ctx carries for the database commits, and reports true; outside one it holds nothing and reports false.

<a name="Database.InTransaction"></a>
### func \(Database\) [InTransaction](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/framework/internal/app/plug/store_interface.go>)

```go
func (Database) InTransaction(ctx context.Context) bool
```

InTransaction reports whether ctx carries a transaction of this database.

<a name="Database.OnAbort"></a>
### func \(Database\) [OnAbort](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/framework/internal/app/plug/store_interface.go>)

```go
func (Database) OnAbort(ctx context.Context, fn func(ctx context.Context)) bool
```

OnAbort holds fn until the work of the scope ctx carries for the database is undone, and reports true; outside one it holds nothing and reports false.

<a name="DatabaseConfig"></a>
## type [DatabaseConfig](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/framework/internal/app/plug/store.go>)

DatabaseConfig is one database a product declares, as the framework opened it: its pool, its dialect, its tuning and the timeout of each call.

```go
type DatabaseConfig struct {
	// Name is the database's, as the product declared it.
	Name         string
	// DB is the pool app.Engine opened.
	DB           *sql.DB
	// Dialect is the engine's SQL dialect: "postgres", "mysql" or
	// "sqlite".
	Dialect      string
	// Timeout bounds each call the framework makes on the database.
	Timeout      time.Duration
	// MaxOpen and MaxIdle bound the pool's connections.
	MaxOpen      int
	// MaxOpen and MaxIdle bound the pool's connections.
	MaxIdle      int
	// MaxLifetime and MaxIdleTime bound a connection's life.
	MaxLifetime  time.Duration
	// MaxLifetime and MaxIdleTime bound a connection's life.
	MaxIdleTime  time.Duration
	// CheckTimeout bounds a check of the database.
	CheckTimeout time.Duration
}
```

<a name="DeadLetterValue"></a>
## type [DeadLetterValue](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/framework/internal/app/plug/queue.go>)

DeadLetterValue is a message its queue gave up on: when, why, and how many times it was delivered.

```go
type DeadLetterValue struct {
	// FailedAt is when its last attempt failed.
	FailedAt   time.Time
	// Reason is the failure's identifier.
	Reason     string
	// Cause is the failure's public text, "" for none.
	Cause      string
	// Message is the message, unmodified.
	Message    MessageValue
	// Code is the failure's error code, 0 for none.
	Code       uint32
	// Deliveries counts its deliveries.
	Deliveries int
}
```

<a name="Documents"></a>

```go
type Documents interface {

	Current(ctx context.Context, key string) (json.RawMessage, error)

	VersionList(ctx context.Context, key string) ([]VersionValue, error)
}
```

<a name="JobDriverConfig"></a>
## type [JobDriverConfig](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/framework/internal/app/plug/jobs.go>)

JobDriverConfig is what framework/app/jobs plugs into kit: how a job's schedule is read from its declaration, and how the scheduler that fires the app's jobs opens.

```go
type JobDriverConfig struct {
	// Every is the schedule of a job that runs every period, first one
	// period after the scheduler starts; a period that is not positive is
	// refused.
	Every func(period time.Duration) (JobScheduleFunc, error)
	// Cron is the schedule of a five-field POSIX cron expression, in the
	// process's local time zone; an expression it cannot read is refused.
	Cron  func(expr string) (JobScheduleFunc, error)
	// Open opens the scheduler the app's jobs run on, as cfg says, with no
	// entry yet.

}
```

<a name="JobEntryValue"></a>
## type [JobEntryValue](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/framework/internal/app/plug/jobs.go>)

JobEntryValue is one job as the scheduler fires it: its name, its schedule, and the run.

```go
type JobEntryValue struct {
	// Name names the job; the scheduler refuses a name it holds already.
	Name             string
	// Schedule says when the job runs next.
	Schedule         JobScheduleFunc
	// Run runs the job once; its error is the result's.
	Run              func(ctx context.Context) error
	// Overlap is what a fire does while the job's previous run goes, as the
	// SDK scheduler's OverlapPolicy numbers it: 0 skips it — the zero —, 1
	// runs it beside, 2 replaces the run; the scheduler refuses any other.
	Overlap          uint8
	// StartingDeadline bounds how late a fire may still start; zero is no
	// bound.
	StartingDeadline time.Duration
}
```

<a name="JobResultValue"></a>
## type [JobResultValue](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/framework/internal/app/plug/jobs.go>)

JobResultValue is one decision of the scheduler: a run of a job, or a fire it skipped.

```go
type JobResultValue struct {
	// Name is the job's.
	Name      string
	// Scheduled is the instant the fire was due.
	Scheduled time.Time
	// Started and Finished bound the run; zero for a fire that did not run.
	Started   time.Time
	// Started and Finished bound the run; zero for a fire that did not run.
	Finished  time.Time
	// Missed counts the fires that came due while the scheduler could not
	// fire them, skipped rather than caught up.
	Missed    int
	// Skipped says the fire did not run: a run of the same job was going.
	Skipped   bool
	// Expired says the fire did not run: the scheduler came to it more
	// than the job's starting deadline after its instant.
	Expired   bool
	// Replaced says a newer fire of a job that replaces its runs cancelled
	// this one — before it started when Started is zero.
	Replaced  bool
	// Err is the run's error.
	Err       error
}
```

```go
}
```

<a name="MailDriverConfig"></a>
## type [MailDriverConfig](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/framework/internal/app/plug/mail.go>)

MailDriverConfig is what framework/app/mail plugs into kit: how a mailer's outbox opens, the SDK's verdict on a mail, the transports a mailer hands its mail to, and how the framework tells the spool's refusals apart.

```go
type MailDriverConfig struct {
	// Open opens one mailer's outbox as cfg says, closed until it runs.
	Open      func(cfg *MailSpoolConfig) (MailSpool, error)
	// Validate is the SDK's verdict on a mail: nil when the outbox takes it,
	// else what is wrong with it, in the SDK's public words.
	Validate  func(msg MailValue) error
	// Capture is a transport that delivers nothing and keeps the last
	// message it composed (MailCaptureSource).
	Capture   func() MailSink
	// ParseSMTP reads an SMTP URL — smtp://user:password@host:port?tls=
	// starttls|implicit|none, smtps:// for implicit TLS — as the SDK's
	// SMTP transport would take it.
	ParseSMTP func(url string) (MailRelayValue, error)
	// NewSMTP is the SDK's SMTP transport to relay, which dials nothing
	// until a mail is sent.
	NewSMTP   func(relay *MailRelayValue) (MailSink, error)
	// Refused reports whether err, or an error it wraps, is the spool's or
	// the URL's refusal of kind: the SDK's sentinels stay in the subsystem,
	// and the error keeps the fields the SDK gave it.
	Refused   func(err error, kind MailRefusal) bool
}
```

```go
}
```

<a name="MailSpoolConfig"></a>
## type [MailSpoolConfig](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/framework/internal/app/plug/mail.go>)

MailSpoolConfig is one mailer's outbox: the transport each attempt runs, the app's clock, what the framework hears of its mails, its retries, and where it keeps them — a queue on the database that keeps the mailer's service, a directory, or memory.

```go
	// failure, or dead-letters the mail after its last attempt.
	Transport       func(ctx context.Context, msg MailValue, attempt MailAttemptValue) error
	// Clock is the app's clock, which the spool stamps and waits on.
	Clock           Clock
	// Observe is told each event of each mail.
	Observe         func(e *MailEventValue)
	// Annotate is what the spool keeps of a Send for its deliveries, read
	// from the Send's context.
	Annotate        func(ctx context.Context) map[string]string
	// NewID mints a mail's outbox ID.
	NewID           func() (string, error)
	// Outbox is the queue the spool keeps its mails in on a database —
	// the queue subsystem's, sealed —, nil for a directory or memory.
	Outbox          Broker
	// Database is the database Outbox is on, whose transaction a mail sent
	// in one joins; nil for none.
	Database        Database
	// From is the sender of every mail that names none: the SDK's
	// mail.Address, held as any.
	From            MailValue
	// Dir is the directory the spool keeps its own queue in; with no Outbox
	// and no Dir, the outbox is in memory.
	Dir             string
	// BackoffBase is the wait after a failed attempt, doubled after each,
	// up to BackoffMax.
	BackoffBase     time.Duration
	// BackoffMax bounds the wait after a failed attempt.
	BackoffMax      time.Duration
	// SendTimeout bounds one attempt.
	SendTimeout     time.Duration
	// PollInterval bounds an idle wait.
	PollInterval    time.Duration
	// MaxAttempts is how many attempts a mail gets before it is
	// dead-lettered.
	MaxAttempts     int
	// MaxMessageBytes bounds one mail in the spool's own queue; zero is the
	// spool's own bound.
	MaxMessageBytes int
	// MaxAge is how long after it was queued a mail may still be retried:
	// an attempt that fails later gives it up; zero sets no age.
	MaxAge          time.Duration
	// RetryPermanent retries a mail the receiving server refused for good —
	// an SMTP 5xx reply — like a temporary failure, instead of giving it up
	// at once.
	RetryPermanent  bool
}
```

<a name="OTLPConfig"></a>
## type [OTLPConfig](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/framework/internal/app/plug/otlp.go>)

OTLPConfig is what the framework asks of an export: who produces the telemetry, where it goes, where it waits, its bounds and the app's clock.

```go
type OTLPConfig struct {
	// Clock is the app's clock: the queues stamp and age a batch on it, the
	// retries and each attempt's bound wait on it, the metrics are
	// collected on it.
	Clock         Clock
	// Headers ride on every request to the collector — an Authorization, a
	// tenant —; they are the secret otlp-headers, never shown.
	Headers       map[string]string
	// Send, when set, ships a batch in place of the OTLP/HTTP exporters:
	// the product's own sender. Retryable then classifies its failures.
	Send          func(ctx context.Context, batch OTLPBatchValue) error
	// Retryable classifies a failure of Send: a later attempt may cure it.
	// Unused without Send: the OTLP/HTTP exporters classify their own.
	Retryable     func(err error) bool
	// OnError hears what the export could not keep — a batch of spans or a
	// snapshot its queue refused — and what it could not close; the core
	// logs it. The forwarder counts every batch it loses on its own.
	OnError       func(err error)
	// Service and Version name the producer: the resource's service.name
	// and the instrumentation scope's version.
	Service       string
	// Service and Version name the producer: the resource's service.name
	// and the instrumentation scope's version.
	Version       string
	// Endpoint is the collector's base URL, "http://collector:4318": each
	// signal's path is appended to it. Unused with Send.
	Endpoint      string
	// Dir is the directory the two queues lie in, one subdirectory per
	// signal; "" keeps them in memory, lost at a stop.
	Dir           string
	// WhenFull is what a full queue does with a new batch: OTLPDropOldest,
	// OTLPDropNewest or OTLPBlock.
	WhenFull      string
	// MaxBytes bounds the bytes each queue holds.
	MaxBytes      int64
	// MaxBatches bounds the batches each queue holds.
	MaxBatches    int
	// MaxAge is how long after it was queued a batch may still be sent.
	MaxAge        time.Duration
	// SendTimeout bounds one attempt, and the hand-over of the spans the
	// batch sink exports to their queue.
	SendTimeout   time.Duration
	// Interval is how often the metrics are collected and queued.
	Interval      time.Duration
	// DrainTimeout is how long the batch being sent at a stop may still
	// run; SettleTimeout bounds each acknowledgement once the stop began,
	// and the flush of what the export still holds in memory.
	DrainTimeout  time.Duration
	// DrainTimeout is how long the batch being sent at a stop may still
	// run; SettleTimeout bounds each acknowledgement once the stop began,
	// and the flush of what the export still holds in memory.
	SettleTimeout time.Duration
}
```

<a name="OTLPExporter"></a>
## type [OTLPExporter](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/framework/internal/app/plug/otlp_interface.go>)

OTLPExporter is an app's export, open: where the tracer hands its spans, what the framework records of each unit of work, the loop that sends, and what it counts.

```go
type OTLPExporter interface {
	// Record counts one unit of work the framework observed on node: its
	// operation, how long it took, and whether it failed.
	Record(node string, op string, took time.Duration, failed bool)
	// Run sends the queued batches and collects the metrics until ctx ends;
	// then it flushes what it holds in memory into the queues, lets the

	// Stats is what each signal's queue holds, has sent and has lost.
	Stats() []OTLPStatsValue
}
```

<a name="OTLPStatsValue"></a>
## type [OTLPStatsValue](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/framework/internal/app/plug/otlp.go>)

OTLPStatsValue is what one signal's queue holds, has sent and has lost, with its bounds.

```go
type OTLPStatsValue struct {
	// LastRetryAfterAt is when the collector last imposed a delay; zero
	// when it never did.
	LastRetryAfterAt time.Time
	// Signal is OTLPTraces or OTLPMetrics.
	Signal           string
	// PendingBytes and MaxBytes are the bytes the queue holds and may hold.
	PendingBytes     int64
	// PendingBytes and MaxBytes are the bytes the queue holds and may hold.
	MaxBytes         int64
	// LastRetryAfter is the last delay the collector imposed.
	LastRetryAfter   time.Duration
	// Pending and MaxBatches are the batches the queue holds and may hold.
	Pending          int
	// Pending and MaxBatches are the batches the queue holds and may hold.
	MaxBatches       int
	// Enqueued, Sent and Retries count the batches kept, sent and the
	// attempts made again.
	Enqueued         uint64
	// Enqueued, Sent and Retries count the batches kept, sent and the
	// attempts made again.
	Sent             uint64
	// Enqueued, Sent and Retries count the batches kept, sent and the
	// attempts made again.
	Retries          uint64
	// Dropped, Expired and DeadLettered count the batches lost to a bound,
	// to their age and to a permanent refusal.
	Dropped          uint64
	// Dropped, Expired and DeadLettered count the batches lost to a bound,
	// to their age and to a permanent refusal.
	Expired          uint64
	// Dropped, Expired and DeadLettered count the batches lost to a bound,
	// to their age and to a permanent refusal.
	DeadLettered     uint64
	// Durable reports whether the queue outlives the process: false in
	// memory — no directory, or a platform whose durable queue the SDK
	// refuses.
	Durable          bool
}
```

<a name="QueueConfig"></a>
## type [QueueConfig](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/framework/internal/app/plug/queue.go>)

QueueConfig is what the framework asks of one queue: where it lies, its policy, the app's clock, and for a mailer's outbox the sealing of what it keeps.

```go
type QueueConfig struct {
	// Name names the queue's node in a refusal: the consumer's or the
	// mailer's node ID.
	Name       string
	// Dir is the directory a file queue lies in; with no Database and no
	// Dir, the queue is in memory.
	Dir        string
	// Database keeps the queue, nil when Dir or memory does: a scope the
	// store subsystem's Database opened, whose transaction a publication in
	// it joins.
	Database   Database
	// Table is the queue's table on Database.
	Table      string
	// Policy is how the queue leases, retries and bounds its messages.
	Policy     QueuePolicyValue
	// Clock is the app's clock, which the queue stamps and waits on.
	Clock      Clock
	// Seal, when set, seals every payload on its way in — a mail's, in a
	// mailer's outbox on a database —, and Unseal opens one on its way out;
	// MaxPayload bounds a payload before it is sealed.
	Seal       func(ctx context.Context, payload []byte) ([]byte, error)
	// Unseal is the payload a box holds, the box as it lies when it does
	// not open.
	Unseal     func(ctx context.Context, box []byte) []byte
	// MaxPayload bounds a payload Seal seals.
	MaxPayload int
	// Wrap, when a test sets it, stands in front of the queue the subsystem
	// opens: a func(queue.Broker) queue.Broker of the SDK's queue, which
	// the framework's core does not name. Nil in every app a product builds.
	Wrap       any
}
```

<a name="QueueDriverConfig"></a>
## type [QueueDriverConfig](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/framework/internal/app/plug/queue.go>)

QueueDriverConfig is what framework/app/queue plugs into kit: how a consumer's queue opens, the migration that makes its table on a database, and how a delivery's handler says that no retry can help.

```go
	// directory, or in memory.

	// TableMigration is the migration that makes the queue table on a

	TableMigration func(dialect string, table string, version uint64) (MigrationValue, error)
	// DoNotRetry is err as a delivery's handler returns it when no retry
	// can help: its queue dead-letters the message at once.
	DoNotRetry     func(err error) error
	// NotRetryable reports whether err, a delivery's handler's, says that no
	// retry can help: what DoNotRetry returned, the product's own included.
	NotRetryable   func(err error) bool
}
```

<a name="QueuePolicyValue"></a>

<a name="RenameSpec"></a>
## type [RenameSpec](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/framework/internal/app/plug/store.go>)

RenameSpec is the framework's tables on a database moved to their present names (ADR 0180 step 5): each table — with the tables the document store derives from it, \<table>\_\_\_ix and \<table>\_\_\_vs —, the history of the former version table taken by the present one, and the names that history gives the tables' migrations.

```go
type RenameSpec struct {
	// FormerVersions is the version table the framework's set had: the move
	// holds its migration lock, is recorded there, and drops it once the
	// history is the present table's.
	FormerVersions string
	// Versions is the version table the framework's set has now.
	Versions       string
	// Name labels the move in FormerVersions, at Version.
	Name           string
	// Tables are the tables moved, each from its former name to its present
	// one.
	Tables         []RenameValue
	// Labels are the names of the tables' migrations in the history, each
	// from what the former release recorded to what this one says.
	Labels         []RenameValue
	// Version is the move's version in FormerVersions: above every version
	// the framework gives.
	Version        uint64
}
```

<a name="StoreConfig"></a>
## type [StoreConfig](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/framework/internal/app/plug/store.go>)

StoreConfig is what the framework asks of one store's engine: the store, its key and its indexes over documents, where it rests and what it keeps, and how its writes take part in the framework's transactions.

```go
type StoreConfig struct {
	// Name is the store's, as a log line and a rollback name it.
	Name        string
	// Key is a document's key: the product's key function on its type,
	// wrapped once at the declaration. It reads the document's Value, which
	// the engine decodes first unless KeyAtRest gives the key.
	Key         func(d DocumentValue) string
	// KeyAtRest, when set, gives the key of a record as it rests, without
	// decoding it; false when it cannot.
	KeyAtRest   func(raw json.RawMessage) (string, bool)
	// Decode is the entity a document's JSON holds, which the engine keeps
	// as the document's Value.
	Decode      func(raw json.RawMessage) (any, error)
	// Indexes are the store's secondary indexes.
	Indexes     []IndexSpec
	// Data is the data directory the store rests in — the SDK's writable
	// file system, which the engine asserts — and Path its snapshot there;
	// a nil Data and a nil Database keep the store in memory.
	Data        fs.FS
	// Path is the store's snapshot in Data.
	Path        string
	// Database keeps the store, nil when the data directory or memory does:
	// a scope the store subsystem's Database opened.
	Database    Database
	// Table is the store's table on Database.
	Table       string
	// IndexKey is the key a table's index keys are hashed under, nil for
	// none: an index key reaches the table as its keyed hash.
	IndexKey    func(index string, key string) []byte
	// Call is the context one call of the engine on Database runs with: on
	// the transaction ctx carries for it, else on the pool, within the
	// database's timeout; done ends it.
	Call        func(ctx context.Context, write bool) (call context.Context, done func(), err error)
	// Versions is how many former versions of each record the engine keeps,
	// none when zero; Clock stamps them.
	Versions    int
	// Clock is the app's clock, which stamps a version.
	Clock       func() time.Time
	// Held reports whether a record's versions are held, and no write may
	// prune them: asked with the write's context, on a database inside its
	// transaction.
	Held        func(ctx context.Context, key string) bool
	// Stamp is what a write under ctx says about the version it makes.
	Stamp       func(ctx context.Context) StampValue
	// Transaction is the framework's transaction, which the engine's writes take part
	// in.
	Transaction Transaction
}
```

<a name="StoreDriverConfig"></a>
## type [StoreDriverConfig](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/framework/internal/app/plug/store.go>)

StoreDriverConfig is what framework/app/store plugs into kit: how a store's engine opens, how the framework opens its scope on a database, and the migration that makes one of the framework's tables.

```go
type StoreDriverConfig struct {
	// Open opens the engine of one store, as cfg places it: loaded from the
	// data directory, empty in memory, or on a database.
	Open           func(cfg StoreConfig) (StoreEngine, error)
	// Database opens the framework's scope on one database's pool.
	Database       func(cfg DatabaseConfig) (Database, error)
	// TableMigration is the migration that makes the table t on a database
	// of the dialect named, at version.
	TableMigration func(dialect string, t TableSpec, version uint64) (MigrationValue, error)
	// FormerTables are the tables of plan still under a former name on db —
	// its former version table among them —, read from the database's
	// catalogue, sorted: what RenameTables would move; none once moved.
	FormerTables   func(ctx context.Context, db Database, plan RenameSpec) ([]string, error)
	// RenameTables moves the tables of plan to their present names on db
	// (ADR 0180 step 5), under the migration lock of plan's former version
	// table and in the transaction that records the move there, and returns
	// the tables it moved; none when nothing was left under a former name.
	// A table whose present name is taken too is a [RefusalRenameTarget],
	// and nothing moves.
	RenameTables   func(ctx context.Context, db Database, plan RenameSpec) ([]string, error)
}
```

<a name="StoreEngine"></a>
## type [StoreEngine](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/framework/internal/app/plug/store_interface.go>)

StoreEngine is what a store runs on, over documents (ADR 0179 §2): the non-generic engine under Store\[T]. Its refusals are the framework's ([Refusal](#Refusal)): the engine translates the SDK's before they reach the core. Every call takes the caller's context, which carries the transaction the call joins. It grows by the sibling interfaces below, never by a method (the SDK's ADR 0039).

```go
type StoreEngine interface {
	// Close releases the engine.
	Close() error
	// Count says how many documents the store holds.
	Count(ctx context.Context) (int, error)
	// Delete removes the document under key.
	Delete(ctx context.Context, key string) error
	// Entries returns up to limit documents as they rest, in key order.
	Entries(ctx context.Context, limit int) ([]json.RawMessage, error)
	// Filter returns the documents keep accepts, in key order.
	Filter(ctx context.Context, keep func(d DocumentValue) bool) ([]DocumentValue, error)
	// Find returns the documents an index files under key, in key order.
	Find(ctx context.Context, index string, key string) ([]DocumentValue, error)
	// Get returns the document under key.
	Get(ctx context.Context, key string) (DocumentValue, error)
	// List returns every document, in key order.
	List(ctx context.Context) ([]DocumentValue, error)
	// Lookup returns the document a unique index files under key.
	Lookup(ctx context.Context, index string, key string) (DocumentValue, error)
	// Update applies fn to the document under key and stores the result,
	// atomically with respect to every other write of the store.
	Update(ctx context.Context, key string, fn func(d *DocumentValue) error) (DocumentValue, error)
	// Watch registers the functions told the key of every document written
	// and deleted, once the write stands.
	Watch(onWrite func(key string), onDelete func(key string))
	// Write stores d as mode says. The document and its index keys are kept
	// together, or neither.
	Write(ctx context.Context, d DocumentValue, mode WriteMode) error
}
```

<a name="StudioDriverConfig"></a>
## type [StudioDriverConfig](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/framework/internal/app/plug/studio.go>)

StudioDriverConfig is what framework/app/studio plugs into kit: how the tool's variables are read, and how the Studio's routes mount.

```go
type StudioDriverConfig struct {
	// Env reads what the tool's variables ask of the Studio in this run.
	Env      func(getenv func(string) string) StudioEnvValue
	// Settings are the tool's variables as the settings of a run show them,
	// in order, each with its value as the run resolved it and where it
	// came from: the product's code, the environment, or the framework's default.
	Settings func(getenv func(string) string, state StudioStateValue) []model.Setting
	// Forced are the variables kit dev says it set itself for this launch,
	// as it names them; the framework labels only those it lets kit dev set.
	Forced   func(getenv func(string) string) []string
	// DevBuild is what kit dev said about the build it launched, nil when
	// the process was not started by kit dev.
	DevBuild func(getenv func(string) string) *model.DevBuild
	// Mount registers the Studio's routes on mux, each behind the Studio's
	// guard, reading the running app through host.
	Mount    func(mux *http.ServeMux, host StudioHost)
}
```

<a name="StudioEnvValue"></a>

<a name="StudioHost"></a>
## type [StudioHost](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/framework/internal/app/plug/studio_interface.go>)

StudioHost is the running app, as the Studio's routes read it and answer through it.

```go
type StudioHost interface {
	// AllowedHost reports whether a request's Host, its port, brackets and
	// case removed, may reach the Studio.
	AllowedHost(host string) bool
	// Databases are the app's databases, each checked and its migrations
	// read again now.
	Databases(ctx context.Context) []model.Database
	// Debug logs, at the debug level, a failure nobody is told of.
	Debug(ctx context.Context, message string, err error)
	// Fail answers an internal error, saying message and nothing of the
	// error.
	Fail(w http.ResponseWriter, message string)
	// Forbid answers that the caller may not reach the Studio, saying
	// message.
	Forbid(w http.ResponseWriter, message string)
	// Former are the former values of the record under key in store, as
	// the Studio's data view shows them.
	Former(ctx context.Context, store string, key string) (model.RecordHistory, error)
	// Graph is the app's graph, as it is now.
	Graph() *model.Graph
	// Instances are a workflow's entities and where each is; false for no
	// such workflow.
	Instances(workflow string) ([]model.Instance, bool)
	// Invalid is the framework's answer to a request the caller must change, saying
	// message.
	Invalid(message string) error
	// Items are a store's latest entities, redacted as payloads are; false
	// for no such store.
	Items(store string) ([]json.RawMessage, bool)
	// Locate says where the function fn, at file:line, lies in the
	// product's own module; nil anywhere else.
	Locate(file string, line int, fn string) *model.Source
	// Logs are the latest records the product logged, those of a trace or
	// a node and from a level when given, at most limit — a default when
	// it is empty; a level or a limit the app does not take is refused.
	Logs(trace string, node string, level string, limit string) ([]model.LogRecord, error)
	// Mail is one mail, whole when its mailer keeps bodies; false when no
	// mailer remembers it.
	Mail(id string) (model.MailMessage, bool)
	// Mails are every mailer's latest mails, at most limit of each.
	Mails(limit int) []model.MailSummary
	// NotFound is the framework's answer to a request for what does not exist,
	// saying message.
	NotFound(message string) error
	// Now is the time on the app's clock.
	Now() time.Time
	// Phase is where the app is in its life, as the graph says it.
	Phase() string
	// Privacy is what the Studio's Privacy page shows.
	Privacy(ctx context.Context) (model.Privacy, error)
	// ProfileUnreadable is the framework's refusal of a profile the process could
	// not read: public says which, cause why, for the logs.
	ProfileUnreadable(public string, cause error) error
	// Remote reports whether the Studio answers a client that is not on
	// this machine.
	Remote() bool
	// Reply answers r with body, a JSON document, or with err as the framework
	// answers an error.
	Reply(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request, body json.RawMessage, err error)
	// Revisions are the versions of the record under key in store, and
	// what changed from version from to version to when both are given.
	Revisions(ctx context.Context, store string, key string, from string, to string) (model.RecordVersions, error)
	// Source is a file the graph names, of the product's Go module or of
	// the one module names: a regular file within the bound, never a link;
	// false for any other name.
	Source(ctx context.Context, module string, file string) ([]byte, bool)
	// Stopping is closed when the app ends its live streams.
	Stopping() <-chan struct{}
	// Stores reports whether the app runs on the store subsystem: the
	// Studio's routes on the stores and the databases are mounted only then.
	Stores() bool
	// Subscribe streams the app's live events until cancel is called.
	Subscribe() (events <-chan model.Event, cancel func())
	// Trace is one trace, while the app keeps it.
	Trace(id string) (model.Trace, bool)
	// Traces are the latest traces the app keeps, at most limit, those of
	// root's trace or through node when either is given.
	Traces(limit int, root string, node string) []model.Trace
	// Trash is a page of store's trash, from offset and at most limit
	// records — defaults when they are empty.
	Trash(ctx context.Context, store string, offset string, limit string) (model.StoreTrash, error)
}
```

<a name="Ticker"></a>
## type [Ticker](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/framework/internal/app/plug/queue_interface.go>)

Ticker is a ticker of a [Clock](#Clock).

```go
type Ticker interface {
	// C receives the clock's instant at each tick.
	C() <-chan time.Time
	// Reset makes the ticker fire every d.

	// Stop stops the ticker.
	Stop()
}
```

<a name="Transaction"></a>
## type [Transaction](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/framework/internal/app/plug/store_interface.go>)

Transaction is the framework's transaction as a store's engine takes part in it (ADR 0139, ADR 0178): the core implements it, an engine calls it with its caller's context.

```go
type Transaction interface {
	// AtCommit holds fn until the transaction ctx carries commits, and
	// reports whether it did: false outside one, where the caller runs it
	// now.
	AtCommit(ctx context.Context, fn func()) bool
	// Local reports whether ctx runs in a transaction that holds the data's
	// writer turn: a write in the data directory or in memory then records
	// what it replaces.
	Local(ctx context.Context) bool
	// Retell keeps fn, which announces a write on a database again when the
	// transaction ctx carries rolls it back.
	Retell(ctx context.Context, fn func())
	// Undo keeps restore, which a rollback of the transaction ctx carries
	// runs; nothing outside one. store names the store in a log line.
	Undo(ctx context.Context, store string, restore func(ctx context.Context) error)
}
```



<a name="TransitionSpec"></a>
## type [TransitionSpec](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/framework/internal/app/plug/workflow.go>)

TransitionSpec declares one transition: an event's, a timer's after a delay or at an instant the entity carries, or a guard's.

```go
type TransitionSpec struct {
	// Instant is when a deadline's transition comes due, false for no
	// instant for now; set for WorkflowTriggerDeadline.
	Instant func(e WorkflowEntityValue) (time.Time, bool)
	// Guard is the condition a guard's transition waits for; set for
	// WorkflowTriggerGuard.
	Guard   func(e WorkflowEntityValue) bool
	// Event names the transition.
	Event   string
	// From is the state it leaves.
	From    string
	// To is the state it enters.
	To      string
	// Delay is how long a delay's transition waits in From.
	Delay   time.Duration
	// Trigger is what fires it: an event, a delay, a deadline or a guard.
	Trigger WorkflowTrigger
}
```

```go
}
```

```go
type WorkflowChangeValue struct {

	// Entity is the entity, as stored after the transition.
	Entity  WorkflowEntityValue
	// Key is the entity's key.
	Key     string
	// Event is the transition's name; WorkflowCreateEvent for Start.
	Event   string
	// From is the state left, "" on creation.
	From    string
```

<a name="WorkflowConfig"></a>
## type [WorkflowConfig](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/framework/internal/app/plug/workflow.go>)

WorkflowConfig is one workflow as its engine runs it: its states and transitions, its hooks, the store and the journal it runs over, and how the app's loop, clock and spans see it.

```go
type WorkflowConfig struct {
	// Store is the workflow's entities, as the engine reads and writes them.
	Store        WorkflowStore
	// Journal keeps what the engine knows of each entity — its state, since
	// when, its latest transitions —; nil keeps it in memory alone.
	Journal      WorkflowJournal
	// Clock is the app's clock, which the engine stamps and waits on.
	Clock        Clock
	// Actor names, from the context of a transition someone fired, who
	// fired it.
	Actor        func(ctx context.Context) string
	// Observe brackets each transition the loop fires: the context it runs
	// with, and the function told how it ended.
	Observe      func(ctx context.Context, f WorkflowFiringValue) (context.Context, func(err error))
	// Report receives what the engine reports and no caller's return value
	// carries: an OnTransition hook that failed, a panic, a journal's write
	// that failed.
	Report       func(ctx context.Context, err error)
	// OnLoop is told each run of the loop, and each wait.
	OnLoop       func(e WorkflowLoopEventValue)
	// Initial is the state Start enters an entity in.
	Initial      string
	// Transitions are the declared transitions, in declaration order.
	Transitions  []TransitionSpec
	// OnEnter are the hooks run as an entity enters a state, in
	// declaration order.
	OnEnter      []EnterHookSpec
	// OnTransition are the hooks run after every stored transition, in
	// declaration order.
	OnTransition []func(ctx context.Context, c WorkflowChangeValue) error
	// MinGap is the least a wake for a due transition waits after a run.
	MinGap       time.Duration
	// BackoffBase is the wait after a run that failed, doubled after each,
	// up to BackoffMax.
	BackoffBase  time.Duration
	// BackoffMax bounds the wait after a run that failed.
	BackoffMax   time.Duration
	// MaxHistory caps the transitions remembered per entity.
	MaxHistory   int
}
```

<a name="WorkflowEngine"></a>
## type [WorkflowEngine](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/framework/internal/app/plug/workflow_interface.go>)

WorkflowEngine is one workflow's engine as the framework's core uses it: the transitions code fires, what a write of the store tells it, what it counts and records, and its loop.

```go
type WorkflowEngine interface {

	Census() map[string]int
	// Changed tells the engine the entity under key was written.

	// Deleted tells the engine the entity under key was deleted.

	// Fire moves the entity under key along the event's transition leaving
	// its state.
	Fire(ctx context.Context, key string, event string) (WorkflowEntityValue, error)
	// Records are what the engine knows of each entity.
	Records() []WorkflowRecordValue
	// Run runs the loop that fires the timers and the guards, until ctx
	// ends.
	Run(ctx context.Context) error
	// Start enters e in the workflow, in the initial state: its OnEnter
	// hooks run, then it is inserted in the store.
	Start(ctx context.Context, e WorkflowEntityValue) (WorkflowEntityValue, error)
}
```

<a name="WorkflowStore"></a>
## type [WorkflowStore](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/framework/internal/app/plug/workflow_interface.go>)

WorkflowStore is the port a workflow's engine reads and writes its entities through: the workflow's store.

```go
type WorkflowStore interface {
	// All yields every entity of the store.
	All(ctx context.Context) iter.Seq2[WorkflowEntityValue, error]
	// Get reads the entity under key; false when there is none.
	Get(ctx context.Context, key string) (WorkflowEntityValue, bool, error)
	// Insert writes e unless its key is taken; false when it was.
	Insert(ctx context.Context, e WorkflowEntityValue) (bool, error)
	// Key is e's key.
	Key(e WorkflowEntityValue) string
	// Replace writes e over the entity of its key; false when there was
	// none.
	Replace(ctx context.Context, e WorkflowEntityValue) (bool, error)
}
```
